Re: H.R. 4888, Mammography Quality Standards Reauthorization Act of 2002
Dear Congressman Dingell:

On behalf of the Susan G. Komen Breast Cancer Foundation, | am writing to
thank you for your leadership in introducing the Mammography Quality Standards
Reauthorization Act of 2002. The Komen Foundation commends you for your efforts in
bringing this important issue into the nation's consciousness and for your commitment to
ensuring that all women in this country have access to early detection.

The Komen Foundation, a leading catalyst in the fight against breast cancer, is
comprised of 116 Affiliates nationwide, and 3 international Affiliates, with over 75,000
volunteers. Since its inception in 1982, Komen has raised more than $450 million in
furtherance of its mission—to eradicate breast cancer as a life-threatening disease by
advancing research, education, screening and treatment. Komen dedicates millions of
dollars annually towards scientific and community outreach projects. The Komen
Foundation Research Program has awarded more than 700 grants, totaling more than
$90 million for breast cancer research. Last year, Komen awarded more than $20.4
million in grants to support institutions conducting cutting-edge imaging technology
research. In addition, Komen Affiliates have funded hundreds of non-duplicative,
community-based breast health education and breast cancer screening and treatment
projects for the medically underserved.

Early detection of breast cancer saves lives. Mammography screening remains
the gold standard in the early detection of breast cancer. In the past decade, breast
cancer mortality rates have declined in the United States. This is due, in large measure,
to early detection and timely treatment. Mammography screening, to reduce breast
cancer mortality, must be sensitive enough to detect the disease. The MQSA
established a national standard of mammography care. Since enactment of the MQSA,
women throughout the country have gained further canfidence in their mammograms, as
well as in those individuals and facilities that provide services as part of screening for
breast cancer.

Given the importance of quality mammography screening in the fight against
breast cancer, the Komen Foundation a!so supports adequate reimbursement for costs

The Komen Foundation applauds your efforts in advancing an issue of utmost
importance, and we offer our deepest appreciation for your continued commitment to
ensuring access to quality care for all Americans.
